review: 1:2 וְנִבְזֶה — Isaiah 53:3 (נִבְזֶה וַחֲדַל אִישִׁים); the Arabic وَأُهِين is 'and despised', and the Hebrew keeps the prophet's participle of the Servant.

2:3 נִקְרַע … הַפָּרֹכֶת — Matthew 27:51 (וַתִּקָּרַע פָּרֹכֶת הַהֵיכָל); the Arabic شُقَّ ذٰلِكَ الْحِجَاب is that veil torn, and פָּרֹכֶת is the temple word, so the sign stays tied to the sanctuary rather than a general curtain.

2:1–2:4 חָשַׁךְ … נִבְקְעוּ … נִקְרַע … נִפְתְּחוּ — the four signs of Matt 27:45–52 in the Arabic order; the Hebrew keeps all four as niphal passives so the stanza reads as one chain of divine passives.

4:1 מְחַיֵּה עָפָר — the Arabic مُحْيِي الرَّمِيم is 'the Enlivener of the dust/corruption'; the Hebrew keeps the concrete עָפָר (dust, as in Dan 12:2, יְשֵׁנֵי עֲפַר־אֲדָמָה) rather than an abstract 'the dead'.

6:1–6:2 וַיַּעַל עַל־כִּסֵּא רָם / מַפְגִּיעַ — Psalm 110:1 with Hebrews 7:25 (מַפְגִּיעַ בַּעֲדָם); the Arabic وَاعْتَلَى الْعَرْشَ … شَافِعًا is that session and intercession, and the glossary term מַפְגִּיעַ is kept.

5:3–5:4 מְקַיֵּם צֶדֶק … כּוֹבֵשׁ — the Arabic مُوفِيًا عَدْلَ الْقَدِير / قَاهِرًا جَيْشَ الْعِدَى is 'fulfilling the Almighty's justice, conquering the army of foes'; the Hebrew keeps both participles, since the resurrection is presented as justice kept and enemies defeated.
